summary: A July 1950 report says an 85-ft fire tower was cleared for and delivered to Long Pine Key; no source found confirms it was built or describes it today.

events.note: July 1950 report: site cleared for an 85-foot tower, to be in operation the next season. The report says the tower was delivered and erection bids were still to be opened; it does not confirm erection.

evidence.supports: Plan: site cleared for an 85-foot fire tower; park superintendent Dan Beard
evidence.quote: The site is cleared for immediate erection of an 85-foot fire tower at Long Pine Key in Everglades National Park, reports Superintendent Dan Beard.

evidence.supports: Tower delivered to the site; erection bids still to be opened
evidence.quote: The tower has been delivered to the site, and the bids of private companies for its erection will be opened next week.

evidence.supports: Purpose: prevent fires like the spring fire that ravaged the section
evidence.quote: The tower will be in operation next season to help prevent disastrous fires such as the one that ravaged that section this spring, Beard says.

evidence.supports: Coverage: Long Pine Key, Paradise Key and the east section of the park
evidence.quote: The tower will afford protection to the Long Pine Key, Paradise Key and east section of the park

evidence.supports: Alternative 60-foot tower at the Humble Oil well road, if funds allow
evidence.quote: If funds are available, a 60-foot tower will be erected this summer at the end of the Humble Oil well road seven miles south of Tamiami Trail.

evidence.supports: Long Pine Key is second-growth pine inside Everglades National Park
evidence.quote: of second growth pine inside Everglades National Park on Long Pine Key

evidence.supports: Long Pine Key is a remnant of second-growth pine (report wording)
evidence.quote: small remnant of 19,840 acres of second growth pine

sources.title: Lone Pine Key - FOREST LOOKOUTS (1950 item transcribed from the Homestead Leader-Enterprise)
Fire History and Fire Records for Everglades National Park (report T-619)

notes_for_editor: Only a 1950 report is documented (tower delivered, erection bids pending). No source confirms the tower was built, when it came down, or describes it today. height_m 25.9 is the 85-foot planned height, not a confirmed built height. The NPS T-619 report mentions two 1951 lookout stations overlooking sawgrass without naming them; it does not link them to this site, so they are left out. A Florida Memory photo titled Pinelands viewed from Long Pine Key fire tower (floridamemory.com/items/show/267808) was blocked (403) for fetch_text and WebFetch and is not cited. The anyplaceamerica.com Long Pine Key Lookout Tower listing was also not reachable. oldgrowthforest.net and the Yumpu copy of T-619 were checked; neither mentions a tower.
